content:
Looks interesting. The latest ChatGPT update adds a Mac integration: you can handle conversations directly within the Apple Messages app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now has an Apple Messages extension.

The new Apple Messages extension lets ChatGPT read and search your chat history on Mac, as well as compose and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available for all ChatGPT macOS desktop app plans and supports both ChatGPT and Codex.

Given the scope of permissions involved, this feature naturally raises concerns about privacy and control. OpenAI emphasises that sending messages requires user approval by default. Users should think carefully before granting permanent approval. OpenAI's extension guidelines detail the related risks, how to revoke permissions, and a known issue involving bypassing the approval prompt.

At this stage, this feature is only available on Macs with Apple Silicon; Intel models are not supported.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, the system will pop up a confirmation prompt before sending. You can also choose to skip this confirmation step in individual conversations.

Looking for this new feature within ChatGPT? The link below can take you directly to the Messages extension page for ChatGPT for Mac.

Collaborative website editing, conversation snapshot sharing, and more

Although the Messages extension is the headline new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now be synced between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, letting users access important conversations on Mac and iPhone at any time.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots will not change after the original conversation is updated.

Links generated from personal accounts can be opened by anyone with the URL; however, workspace links can only be opened by members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex will mask known sensitive formats, but reminds users to check their own snapshots, as they may still contain sensitive data.

Additionally, website owners can invite existing members of the same workspace to co-edit websites with collaboration enabled. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish updates once the owner has completed the initial publish. Owners retain control over access permissions, settings, analytics, and version rollback.

Some website owners can also change URLs hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, with old addresses automatically redirecting to the new address.

Finally, the computer use history feature launched last week is now being expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. This opt-in feature requires the memory feature to be enabled to work and is off by default.

You can see the full release notes for this update here.
